cells.tense: Here, with the pen, you are asking, listening, and holding at the same time.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you have been holding back from a person who has earned it, and name the boundary after.
cells.core:
You ask because you actually want to know, and you can carry the answers without buckling. Someone else in a hard spot goes flat or goes rigid; you stay curious and stay standing. That is not ordinary. Curiosity usually gets sold out the moment weight shows up, and yours has not.

The weight is really there, so the risk is not that you will break. It is that the asking becomes another thing you are good at taking on. Keep the questions pointed at what matters. If they stop pointing, the listening goes slack and the strength turns into simply carrying. What serves the load is staying in the room with it, not disappearing into it.
cells.sheetLine: Curiosity that can carry weight, not just withstand it.
cells.verb: Listening and questioning your way into what you already half know.
cells.place: Under a load that has to hold, where there is no soft place to put it down.

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future where the load already broke, ahead of its arrival.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you are doing, without building the case and without forecasting the ending.
cells.core:
You are living in a version of this that has not happened yet. The load is coming, or it might be, so you brace — you ask harder, you brace the answer before it lands, you hold a shape that nothing has actually filled. That is more weight than the present has handed you, and the bracing eats the same strength that bearing the present would need.

Bearing weight is real work. The object is early. Endurance works on what is actually on your back; you are carrying what might land on someone's shoulders next. If the brace is not aimed, it spreads. Set it down long enough to see the room you are in. Then pick it up again only where there is something to lift.
cells.sheetLine: Carrying a weight that has not arrived yet.
cells.verb: Listening and questioning your way into what you already half know.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Ask someone one question you do not know the answer to, and stay for the answer.
cells.core:
The questions stopped. You are not out of things to know, and you are not out of strength. The asking is not happening, and the load sits there unexamined while you bear it by bracing. A braced grip is not the same as a bearable one, and it will not hold as much.

The curiosity was real, and it has not gone. It is just pointed away from anyone who might answer. You bear a lot; bearing it alone is a different grip, and you have been using that one. What lets you bear more is going toward the room, not staying braced for it. Start with a question small enough to keep and see what the answer does.

cells.tense: You are already bearing and still asking, and you keep calling it just being practical.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have been calling someone else's call, out loud, once.
cells.core:
The learning is running — you watch, you notice, you adjust the grip — and you file it under carrying the load. The questions are part of the bearing, and the bearing is doing the asking, so it is hard to see where one ends and the other begins. People benefit from the version they get, and the version they get comes from you.

There is a difference between bearing weight and the kind that makes the bearing possible. You keep doing the second and only reporting the first. Nothing here needs to be announced to a room. It needs to be claimed by the one person whose grip it is. When you call it just bearing, the thing that makes bearing work gets no credit and cannot be strengthened on purpose.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has a 'room where saying it didn't go well' — the record does not carry their history, so the Too Little cell must stay on the observable mechanics of a stopped offering, not narrate what happened. A reader could reasonably say the card is about wisdom, not about endurance, and that the seat is being over-read as strain when Fortitude also means resilient strength; the cells must hold the seat as capacity that bends rather than as only pressure. The ask survives being wrong because each one is an act a camera could see, useful even if the read misses, and never conditional on the person obeying it. The sentence that would serve me rather than them is any line that praises a method I invented for them — cut.
